title: legal redlines scratchpad — enterprise contracts
content:
Legal redlines scratchpad — quick notes and bullets (notes to self)

Context: personal scratchpad for common clauses we see in enterprise NDAs/MSAs/SaaS agreements when sales asks for ’standard customer edits’. Mostly shorthand for negotiation talking points and fallback language.

Clauses to watch (priority order):
- Liability / damages cap: target = lesser of $X or 12 months fees. push back on unlimited/liquidated damages, consequential damages carveouts.
- Indemnity: avoid overly broad third-party claims tied to customer content; prefer mutual IP indemnity (we indemnify for model IP infringement; customer indemnifies for their data/outputs).
- Data/use of customer data: no right to use customer data for model training by default. If customer insists, require explicit opt-in, narrow scope, audit trail, and compensation.
- Confidentiality: ensure machine-readable outputs from model treated as customer confidential if derived from customer prompt + private data. Carve out public domain and aggregated de-identified metrics.
- Security & compliance: SOC2 + encryption-in-transit+at-rest baseline. For Private/VPC deployments: add KMS/HSM controls and on-prem deployment specifics.
- Subprocessing / subcontractors: require notice + right to object for named subprocessors doing sensitive work. For hosted API, list typical cloud providers.
- Audit rights: limit to annual, scoped to our SOC2 controls, with cost-shifting if frequent or expansive. No live system debugging by customer without SRE escort.
- Termination / transition assistance: define reasonable transition period and fees; ensure we can retain logs for incident response per retention policy.
- SLA / credits: avoid hard availability SLAs for experimental models; for Dedicated we can commit to SLAs. Credits should be capped and not compound with other remedies.
- Export control / sanctions: standard compliance language; right to suspend if legal/regulatory issues.

Negotiation talking points (sales-friendly, short):
- "We can grant a narrow, revocable training usage right if necessary, but it must be scoped and compensated — this protects both parties."
- "Our liability cap aligns to fees paid because it correlates to the commercial relationship; unlimited liability would kill feasibility for large-scale inference workloads."
- "We already have SOC2 + annual pen tests; for add’l controls we offer Private deployments or dedicated instances with customer-managed keys."
- "We treat customer prompt/response pairs as confidential when marked/derived from customer data — want to make sure outputs aren't reused for model training unless you opt in."

Suggested fallback language snippets (copyable):
- Liability cap: "Supplier's aggregate liability arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) the total Fees paid by Customer under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding the claim; or (ii) $250,000."
- Training opt-in: "Customer grants Supplier a limited, revocable license to use Customer Data solely to improve Supplier's models subject to separate written agreement and compensation."
- Confidential outputs: "Outputs generated by the Service that are derived from Customer Data shall be treated as Confidential Information of Customer."

Practical checklist for sales/legal handoff:
- Is this Hosted / Dedicated / Private? (changes exposure and controls)
- Any customer-specific regulatory regime? (HIPAA, FedRAMP, GDPR special needs)
- Export/sanctions risk (customer country + end-use)
- Any ask for training rights? mark as high risk and escalate.
- Requested changes to indemnity or IP? escalate to me + engineering for feasibility.

Open questions / items to resolve: (notes to self)
- Need standard clause for "model explainability" requests — how to handle operator-provided debugging data vs customer IP.
- Work with infra on realistic guaranteed retention windows for logs for audit/incident response.
- Draft short playbook section for sales (one-pager) with these fallbacks; link to Confluence redlines playbook.

References / quick links:
- Confluence: Redlines Playbook (linked above)
- Jira: REDWOOD-789 (msas: standard redline requests)
- Slack exec thread: C01ABCDEF (customer X: heavy training ask)

Notes to self: keep this doc messy — intended as fast reference. Move finalized snippets to the official playbook. When in doubt, escalate to Emma or Priya.

-- Jordan
